# behaviors


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

`answerui.behaviors` generates the delegated event script
(`Registry.build_js`) for handlers registered in `Registry` and defines
`browser.js` to wire up AnswerUI’s shared browser modules.

Application handlers are stored in `Registry` as records containing a
selector, an event name, a capture flag, and a JavaScript handler body.
The generated script installs one `document` listener per event and
capture phase, then matches the nearest ancestor for each rule’s
selector when an event fires. Elements inserted by htmx work without
attaching extra listeners. Built-in interactive controllers with local
state are mounted through a `MutationObserver` in `browser.js` and
disposed when their elements are removed from the document.

``` python
from answerui.registry import reg, hypelt
from fastcore.test import *
```

## The runtime

`_runtime` is the entire client script. `build_js` embeds `rules` as an
array of objects. Each object has `sel` (selector), `evs` (DOM event
names), `cap` (capture boolean), `init` (boolean), and `fn` (handler).
The script groups these objects by event name and capture phase, then
installs one `document` listener per group regardless of how many rules
share it. When an event fires on an `Element` target, that listener
calls `closest(r.sel)` for each rule in the group and runs `r.fn(el, e)`
on any match.

An `init` rule runs when matching elements enter the document. When
`rules` includes any `init` rule, the script registers a callback with
`htmx.onLoad`. htmx calls that callback with `document.body` on initial
load and with the root element of each swapped fragment. The callback
checks `root` itself (`root.matches`) and its descendants
(`root.querySelectorAll`). Checking ancestors instead would re-run
`init` handlers on outer elements already in the page. Each `init` call
passes a synthetic `new Event('init')` that is never dispatched. Load
htmx before this script whenever you register `init` rules. FastHTML’s
default headers and `demo` both include htmx first.

The script executes once per document. FastHTML sends page headers only
with full pages, never with htmx fragment responses. When htmx swaps a
full page, it discards the incoming `<head>`.

Each handler is an `async` function. If one throws, the returned promise
is rejected without stopping other handlers registered for the same
event. Capture-phase listening (`cap=True`) is opt-in for non-bubbling
events such as `toggle` and `scroll`. A regenerated script takes effect
cleanly only in a fresh page or preview. Injecting a second copy into
the same document attaches duplicate listeners alongside the existing
ones.

## Entries

`_entry` formats each behavior record as one object literal in `rules`.
AnswerUI defines two special event names. `init` runs when an element
enters the document. `cleanup` runs before an element is removed by
htmx. Every other name is a DOM event. A leading `:` expands to `htmx:`
(for example, `':after-request'` becomes `'htmx:after-request'`).

htmx dispatches events under three naming conventions. htmx 2 dispatches
camelCase names such as `htmx:afterSwap` together with hyphenated
aliases such as `htmx:after-swap`. htmx 4 uses colon-separated names
such as `htmx:after:swap`. FastHTML’s `htmx4=True` sets `metaCharacter`
to `-`, turning every colon into a hyphen (`htmx-after-swap`). `_event`
normalizes these spellings to `htmx:` followed by the hyphenated name.
`_spellings` expands a canonical htmx event back into all three DOM
event names. The script registers listeners for all three because only
one fires on a given page.

`init` and `cleanup` are handled separately. Because `init` is not a DOM
event, `_spellings('init')` returns `[]` and the script invokes `init`
handlers through `htmx.onLoad` across both htmx versions. For `cleanup`,
`_spellings` returns `_cleanup`, which lists htmx 2’s hyphenated alias
(`htmx:before-cleanup-element`), htmx 4’s `htmx:before:cleanup`, and
FastHTML’s `htmx-before-cleanup`. Under htmx 4, `cleanup` fires only for
elements initialised by htmx (elements with `hx-` attributes). Each
distinct handler body becomes one `async` function taking `(el, e)`,
declared before `rules` and referenced by name in each entry:

`_event` normalizes every htmx event spelling to the same canonical
name. `_spellings` returns the DOM event names registered for it:

``` python
for ev in [':after-swap', 'htmx:afterSwap', 'htmx:after:swap', 'htmx-after-swap']: test_eq(_event(ev), 'htmx:after-swap')
_spellings('htmx:after-swap')
```

    ['htmx:after-swap', 'htmx:after:swap', 'htmx-after-swap']

## Building the script

A behavior is identified by `(selector, canonical_event, capture)`,
using `_event` to canonicalize the event name. Declaring the same
identity again replaces the earlier handler. Only the last declaration
in registry order appears in the script. Because re-registering a rule
preserves its original position in `self.rules`, re-running a component
definition cannot overwrite an application rule registered later.
Replacing a handler also keeps the identity’s original position in the
output dict to preserve execution order. Because `Registry` compares
selector strings literally without parsing CSS, two distinct selectors
matching the same element are separate behaviors. Both handlers run.

`behaviors` returns the effective handler for each identity along with
its declaring `rule` key. `build_js` deduplicates identical handler
bodies and assembles the script:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

``` python
def build_js():
```

*The behavior script: one function per distinct handler, one entry per
effective behavior*

### Registry.behaviors

``` python

```

*The effective behavior per (selector, event, capture): the last
declared in registry order, with the key of the rule that declared it*

This example defines a `NoticeBox` component with two behaviors: an
`init` handler that removes the element after an `autodismiss` delay,
and a `click` handler on `[dismiss]`. Because htmx calls `htmx.onLoad`
only for the initial page and newly swapped fragments, swapping content
inside an existing `notice-box` does not restart its timer:

``` python
NoticeBox = hypelt('NoticeBox', layer='components', doc='A notice that dismisses itself.', on={
    ('&[autodismiss]', 'init'): r"await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, +el.getAttribute('autodismiss'))); el.remove()",
    ('& [dismiss]', 'click'): r"el.closest('notice-box').remove()"})
print('\n'.join(l for l in reg.build_js().splitlines() if 'notice-box' in l))
```

    async function f1(el, e) { el.closest('notice-box').remove() }
    const rules = [{sel: ":is(notice-box)[autodismiss]", evs: [], cap: false, init: true, fn: f0},
    {sel: ":is(notice-box) [dismiss]", evs: ["click"], cap: false, init: false, fn: f1}];

The `init` entry has `init: true` and `evs: []` because `htmx.onLoad`
invokes it instead of a `document` listener. The `click` entry has
`init: false`. `build_js` emits the handler functions and `rules` array.
At page load, the script groups those entries into `document` listeners.

You can register the same handler body for multiple events in one rule.
Here a `form` is marked `dirty` on `input` and on `change` (a `<select>`
fires only `change`). Registering the `input` handler again in an
anonymous rule keeps the `change` handler in place because anonymous
rule keys include their behaviors. `build_js` declares the shared
handler function once and references it from both entries:

``` python
_dirty = r"el.toggleAttribute('dirty', [...el.elements].some(c => c.value !== c.defaultValue))"
reg.rule(name='dirty', sel='form', on={('&', 'input'): _dirty, ('&', 'change'): _dirty})
reg.rule(sel='form', on={('&', 'input'): _dirty})
s = reg.build_js()
test_eq(s.count(_dirty), 1)
test_eq(s.count('":is(form)"'), 2)
```

To require confirmation before dismissing a notice, register the same
selector and event on `NoticeBox`. Just as in the component definition,
`&` expands to `:is(notice-box)`. Because the behavior identity matches,
the confirmation handler replaces the original. Each effective
behavior’s `rule` field holds the key of the rule that supplied its
active handler:

``` python
NoticeBox.rule('confirm-dismiss', on={('& [dismiss]', 'click'): r"if (confirm('Dismiss this notice?')) el.closest('notice-box').remove()"})
{k: b['rule'] for k,b in reg.behaviors().items()}
```

    {(':is(notice-box)[autodismiss]', 'init', False): 'NoticeBox.base',
     (':is(notice-box) [dismiss]', 'click', False): 'NoticeBox.confirm-dismiss',
     (':is(form)', 'input', False): '858472c34654',
     (':is(form)', 'change', False): 'dirty'}

The generated script contains only the confirmation click handler for
`[dismiss]`. `NoticeBox.behaviors` still lists both declarations made on
the component. `reg.behaviors` returns only the effective handlers
emitted to the script:

``` python
s = reg.build_js()
test_eq(s.count('":is(notice-box) [dismiss]"'), 1)
assert 'confirm(' in s
NoticeBox.behaviors
```

      'ev': 'init',
      'js': "await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, +el.getAttribute('autodismiss'))); el.remove()",
      'cap': False},

``` python
    ('& [dismiss]', 'click'): r"el.closest('notice-box').remove()"})
test_eq(reg.behaviors()[(':is(notice-box) [dismiss]', 'click', False)]['rule'], 'NoticeBox.confirm-dismiss')
```

## Built-in browser behavior

`browser.js` connects AnswerUI’s shared JavaScript modules
(`floating.js`, `interactions.js`, `fit.js`, and `copy.js`) to
server-rendered HTML, including fragments inserted by htmx. Native
controls, CSS tooltips, and static surfaces require no JavaScript.

Form helpers attach document-level `input`, `change`, `reset`,
`focusout`, and capture-phase `invalid` listeners:

- `enable(form)` toggles `disabled` on each `button[enable]` from its
  space-separated tokens (`changed` for modified form values, `valid`
  for constraint validity).
- `range(input)` sets `--ui-range-fill` on `input[range]` from `min`,
  `max`, and `value`.
- Changing `input[reveals]` sets `hidden` on the element whose `id`
  matches the attribute value.
- `validity(control, event)` writes native `validationMessage` text into
  a `small[validation][ui-tone="danger"]` child of `[field]`, links it
  via `aria-describedby`, suppresses the browser popup, and focuses the
  first invalid control on submit.

Document-level action handlers cover common UI events:

- Clicking `button[dismiss]` removes the closest `[alert]` or `[toast]`.
- Clicking `button[copy]` or `button[copyfor]` copies text with
  `copyText`, setting `copied` (and `aria-label="Copied"` if an
  `aria-label` exists) for 1500 ms.
- Clicking `button[commandfor]` falls back to `showModal()` for
  `command="show-modal"` and `close()` for `command="close"` when
  `commandForElement` is unavailable.
- On `animationend`, `browser.js` removes `[toast]` elements when
  `ui-toast-lifetime` finishes.
- On htmx swap events (`htmx:after-swap`, `htmx:after:swap`,
  `htmx-after-swap`), `browser.js` calls `showModal()` on a closed
  `dialog[dialog]` when content is swapped inside it.

Stateful controllers are tracked in a `WeakMap` and managed by a
`MutationObserver` on `document.body`. On initial load and for every
added subtree, `mount` handles:

- `[popup][popover]` and `[popovertarget]`: attaches `mountPopover` (and
  `mountHoverPopover` when `[hovercard]` is present), reading
  `data-side`, `data-align`, and `data-side-offset` (default `6`).
- `[tabs]` with `[role=tablist]`: attaches `mountTabs` using
  `data-activation-mode`.
- `[toolbar][role=toolbar]`: attaches `mountToolbar`.
- `[navbar]`: attaches `mountNavbar` when both `nav` and
  `[navbar-toggle]` are present or `[navbar-sticky]` is set.
- `[toaster]`: opens the popover with `showPopover()` when not already
  open.
- `input[range]` and `button[enable]`: runs their initial state updates.

Removing a disconnected element calls its disposer and clears any
pending copy timer. Moving an element within the document keeps
`isConnected` true and preserves its mounted controller.

``` python
_forms = r'''
import {mountPopover} from './floating.js';
import {mountTabs, mountToolbar, mountHoverPopover} from './interactions.js';
import {mountNavbar} from './fit.js';
import {copyText} from './copy.js';

function enable(form) {
  if (!form) return;
  const changed = [...form.elements].some(control => control.matches('input:not([type=hidden], [type=submit], [type=button], [type=reset]), select, textarea') &&
    (control.type === 'checkbox' || control.type === 'radio' ? control.checked !== control.defaultChecked :
      control.tagName === 'SELECT' ? [...control.options].some(option => option.selected !== option.defaultSelected) : control.value !== control.defaultValue));
  const valid = [...form.elements].every(control => control.validity.valid);
  for (const button of form.querySelectorAll('button[enable]'))
    button.disabled = !button.getAttribute('enable').split(' ').every(want => want === 'changed' ? changed : want === 'valid' ? valid : true);
}

function range(input) {
  const low = input.min === '' ? 0 : +input.min, high = input.max === '' ? 100 : +input.max;
  input.style.setProperty('--ui-range-fill', `${high > low ? (input.value - low) / (high - low) * 100 : 0}%`);
}

function validity(control, event) {
  const field = control.closest('[field]');
  if (!field) return;
  let message = field.querySelector(':scope > small[validation]');
  const ids = (control.getAttribute('aria-describedby') || '').split(' ').filter(id => id && id !== message?.id);
  const show = event.type === 'invalid' || (event.type === 'focusout' ? control.matches(':user-invalid') : message && !control.validity.valid);
  if (show) {
    if (!message) {
      message = document.createElement('small');
      message.setAttribute('validation', '');
      message.setAttribute('ui-tone', 'danger');
      message.id = `validation-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 10)}`;
      field.append(message);
    }
    message.textContent = control.validationMessage;
    ids.push(message.id);
  } else message?.remove();
  if (ids.length) control.setAttribute('aria-describedby', ids.join(' '));
  else control.removeAttribute('aria-describedby');
  if (event.type === 'invalid') {
    event.preventDefault();
    if ([...(control.form?.elements ?? [control])].find(item => !item.validity.valid) === control) control.focus();
  }
}

function changed(event) {
  const control = event.target;
  if (!(control instanceof Element)) return;
  if (control.form?.querySelector('button[enable]')) enable(control.form);
  if (control.matches('input[range]')) range(control);
  if (control.matches('input[reveals]')) document.getElementById(control.getAttribute('reveals')).hidden = !control.checked;
  if (control.matches('input, select, textarea')) {
    validity(control, event);
    for (const message of control.form?.querySelectorAll('small[validation]') ?? []) if (!message.closest('[field]')) message.remove();
  }
}
document.addEventListener('input', changed);
document.addEventListener('change', changed);
document.addEventListener('reset', event => setTimeout(() => {
  enable(event.target);
  for (const input of event.target.querySelectorAll('input[range]')) range(input);
}));
for (const type of ['focusout', 'invalid']) document.addEventListener(type, event => {
  if (event.target.matches('input, select, textarea')) validity(event.target, event);
}, {capture: type === 'invalid'});
'''
```

``` python
_actions = r'''
document.addEventListener('click', async event => {
  const button = event.target.closest('button');
  if (!button) return;
  if (button.hasAttribute('dismiss')) button.closest('[alert], [toast]')?.remove();
  if (button.matches('[copy], [copyfor]')) {
    const target = document.getElementById(button.getAttribute('copyfor'));
    const text = button.hasAttribute('copy') ? button.getAttribute('copy') : target?.matches('input, textarea, select') ? target.value : target?.textContent;
    if (text == null) return;
    await copyText(text);
    if (!button.isConnected) return;
    button._label ??= button.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? '';
    button.toggleAttribute('copied', true);
    if (button._label) button.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Copied');
    clearTimeout(button._copied);
    button._copied = setTimeout(() => {
      button.removeAttribute('copied');
      if (button._label) button.setAttribute('aria-label', button._label);
    }, 1500);
  }
  if (button.hasAttribute('commandfor') && !('commandForElement' in button)) {
    const target = document.getElementById(button.getAttribute('commandfor')), command = button.getAttribute('command');
    if (command === 'show-modal') target.showModal();
    else if (command === 'close') target.close();
  }
});
document.addEventListener('animationend', event => {
  if (event.animationName === 'ui-toast-lifetime' && event.target.matches('[toast]')) event.target.remove();
});
for (const type of ['htmx:after-swap', 'htmx:after:swap', 'htmx-after-swap']) document.addEventListener(type, event => {
  const dialog = event.target.closest('dialog[dialog]');
  if (dialog && event.target !== dialog && !dialog.open) dialog.showModal();
});
'''
```

``` python
_mounts = r'''
const mounted = new WeakMap();
const tabs = '[tabs], [tabs] [role=tablist]';
const navbar = '[navbar], [navbar] > [navbar-row], [navbar-row] > nav, [navbar-row] > [navbar-toggle]';
const selector = `${tabs}, ${navbar}, [popup][popover], [popovertarget], [toolbar][role=toolbar], [toaster], input[range], button[enable], [copy], [copyfor]`;
function own(elements, dispose) {
  const stop = () => { dispose(); for (const element of elements) mounted.delete(element); };
  for (const element of elements) mounted.set(element, stop);
}
function mount(element) {
  if (mounted.has(element)) return;
  if (element.matches('[popovertarget]')) {
    const panel = element.popoverTargetElement;
    if (panel?.matches('[popup]')) mount(panel);
  } else if (element.matches('[popup][popover]')) {
    const trigger = document.querySelector(`[popovertarget="${CSS.escape(element.id)}"]`);
    if (!trigger) return;
    const stop = mountPopover(trigger, element, {side: element.dataset.side, align: element.dataset.align, sideOffset: +(element.dataset.sideOffset ?? 6)});
    const hover = element.hasAttribute('hovercard') ? mountHoverPopover(trigger, element) : undefined;
    own([element, trigger], () => { hover?.(); stop(); });
  } else if (element.matches(tabs)) {
    const root = element.closest('[tabs]'), list = root?.querySelector('[role=tablist]');
    if (list && !mounted.has(root)) own([root, list], mountTabs(root, {activationMode: root.dataset.activationMode}).dispose);
  } else if (element.matches('[toolbar][role=toolbar]')) own([element], mountToolbar(element));
  else if (element.matches(navbar)) {
    const root = element.closest('[navbar]'), row = root?.querySelector(':scope > [navbar-row]');
    const nav = row?.querySelector(':scope > nav'), toggle = row?.querySelector(':scope > [navbar-toggle]');
    if (nav && toggle || root?.hasAttribute('navbar-sticky')) {
      mounted.get(root)?.();
      own([root, row, nav, toggle].filter(Boolean), mountNavbar(root).dispose);
    }
  } else if (element.matches('[toaster]')) { if (!element.matches(':popover-open')) element.showPopover(); }
  else if (element.matches('input[range]')) range(element);
  else if (element.matches('button[enable]')) enable(element.form);
}
function cleanup(element) {
  mounted.get(element)?.();
  mounted.delete(element);
  clearTimeout(element._copied);
}
function visit(root, action, match = selector) {
  if (!(root instanceof Element)) return;
  if (root.matches(match)) action(root);
  root.querySelectorAll(match).forEach(action);
}
visit(document.body, mount);
new MutationObserver(records => {
  for (const record of records) for (const node of record.removedNodes) if (!node.isConnected) visit(node, cleanup, '*');
  for (const record of records) for (const node of record.addedNodes) if (node.isConnected) visit(node, mount);
}).observe(document.body, {childList: true, subtree: true});
'''
```
